title: Finite-Larmor-radius vortex interaction from δf to full-f gyrofluid dynamics
byline: Rinner; Manuel; Locker; Franz Ferdinand; Held; Markus; Kendl; Alexander
html:
Abstract:We study finite-size electrostatic gyrofluid vortex pairs in a two-dimensional isothermal model, focusing on finite-Larmor-radius effects and the transition from local perturbative to finite-amplitude full-distribution dynamics. An effective response kernel based on Padé ion gyroaveraging regularizes the short-range Euler interaction on the Larmor-radius scale while preserving its logarithmic far field, yielding a finite- core prediction for the orbital frequency. Local-model scans show that increasing the ion temperature relative to the electron temperature enhances gyrospinning and filamentation and drives a separation-dependent transition from merger to long-lived co-rotation. Long-wavelength simulations reproduce the predicted finite-Larmor- radius-induced dip in orbital angular frequency, corresponding to a pronounced slowdown of the vortex-pair rotation. For the full-distribution regime, we introduce a quasi-neutrality-consistent initialization that reconstructs the ion gyrocenter density from prescribed electron density and electrostatic potential. It recovers the local limit at small amplitude, whereas finite-amplitude simulations reveal additional mean-density polarization vorticity, delayed or arrested merger, and a loss of density- vorticity sign symmetry already in the cold-ion full-f system. An independent sign scan of density and vorticity then shows how this nonlinear NOB asymmetry combines with the local warm-ion FLR symmetry breaking identified in earlier {\delta}f vortex studies; for warm ions, Padé-based arbitrary-wavelength NOB and NOB+LWL polarization additionally produce distinct morphologies and trajectories. These results demonstrate that nonlinear density-dependent polarization and FLR physics form separate but coupled mechanisms that can qualitatively alter elementary vortex interactions in two-dimensional gyrofluid dynamics.
